notes:
Top-level: Velaris builds a mid-market support SaaS (helpdesk + agent-assist). Current stack: React/web agent UI, internal CRM via REST, Postgres for tickets. Exploring Redwood for hosted inference to speed time-to-value; plan: Hosted API POC (4-week) to validate streaming + tool calling for external actions (create ticket, fetch customer profile), then evaluate Dedicated for predictable unit costs after pilot.

Key asks / quotes: "We need streaming that actually pushes first token in under 1.5s at 95th pct with our prod-like load (burst qps ~180)." Product says streaming + function/tool calling is mandatory — tool calls to our ticket API and to a knowledge base vector store.

Security/Sys: SSO/SAML required for console access; audit logging and KMS integration desired. They prefer public cloud/VPC peering for initial pilot. Will need SOC2 or equivalent on roadmap for procurement.

Cost sensitivity: Mid-market buyer; unit-cost matters. CFO flagged model cost vs. ROI (reduction in handle time). They asked for batching/kv cache suggestions — interested in Redwood Optimize recs.

POC success metrics: first-token latency <1.5s 95th, end-to-end tool call latency <600ms, 20% reduction in average handle time in sandbox, stable streaming for 5 concurrent agents per account.

Quote from engineering lead: "If hosted can meet the latency SLO at scale, we can fast-track to Dedicated later for cost predictability. If not, risk building in-house or using other vendors."

Internal notes: AE ran demo (2026-02-18) with streaming and a mock function-calling flow. SE deep-dive 2026-03-03 showed request/response sizes and KV cache opportunities. Security team submitted initial questionnaire (drive link). Finance requested a 3-tier committed pricing example for Dedicated (monthly commit) to model TCO.

Short-hand next steps: schedule POC kickoff (4/1 target), supply test keys & sample dataset, instrument client-side timing traces, provide Dedicated pricing scenarios and SLA draft, follow up on SOC2 evidence.

CRM frags: "Met with CTO; likes dev experience. Demo: streaming looked good but 95th tail needs validation. Finance: wants ARR math. Security: waiting on KMS integration diagram."

use_case_summary: Velaris aims to add a real-time agent-assist layer to their support product: streaming responses for live agents, deterministic function/tool calling for ticket actions and KB lookups, and fallback routing to smaller models when latency spikes. Priority is streaming latency; they require <1.5s first-token SLO at 95th percentile under pilot load. Secondary concern: per-token cost and ability to move to Dedicated for predictable monthly spend.
requirements: support for batching and KV cache
